page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show strong capabilities across multiple domains. The instance achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Passmark CPU and database operations. Memory performance is supported by DDR5 technology, delivering strong write bandwidth for large blocks and strong read bandwidth for cached small blocks, though uncached large block reads fall into the average tier. Cryptographic and integer operations are accelerated by hardware flags such as AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI.

The m7a.8xlarge is highly suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and moderate-scale machine learning tasks. It demonstrates top-tier performance in prompt processing for small language models and strong performance in text generation. Given its dedicated core allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory, it offers a balanced resource profile for enterprise applications, web serving, and data processing without the overhead of specialized GPU hardware.
